page: Microsoft Azure E48bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs via multithreading. The processor is provisioned with 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction sets such as AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 384.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive configurations. Fast temporary storage is provisioned via an integrated 1933 GB local solid-state drive, complemented by support for Premium Storage block devices. Network connectivity is delivered without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and the instance contains no dedicated GPU acceleration hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate upper-quartile performance across memory and multithreaded operations. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 50758.8, PassMark memory score of 2826.39, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 221.85 GB/sec. Synthetic database benchmarks reached 23567.62 operations in PassMark testing and 44.07 million Redis SET operations per second. In contrast, CPU-bound machine learning tasks show performance limits on dense models, recording 2.33 tokens per second on 70B parameter text generation.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides resource density without the expense of specialized GPU nodes. With substantial local NVMe storage and high multi-core throughput, the E48bds_v5 is suitable for enterprise database engines, in-memory caches, distributed analytics, and large ETL data transformation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E48bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine delivering 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 384.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes a 1933 GB local SSD alongside Premium Storage capabilities. The architecture leverages AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets while operating without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded performance, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 15896.0, a PassMark CPU score of 50758.8, and strong throughput in database operations and bzip3 decompression. Single-core benchmarks and large-scale LLM inference show average to poor throughput due to the lack of dedicated accelerator hardware. The configuration offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-dense operations, making it suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching systems, data processing, and large enterprise workloads.
